guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

includeEmpty.description: Include parameters without a value (default true).

limit.description: Maximum number of elements returned (1-200, default 50).

offset.description: Number of elements to skip, for paging (default 0).

tools.name: get_element_relationships
tools.description: How elements relate to others: host (and host face element), group and assembly they belong to (and members when the element is itself a group or assembly), owner view, design option, nested family super/sub-components, hosted inserts (doors/windows/openings of a wall, roof, floor), geometry joins, and optionally dependents (elements Revit deletes with it), filtered by category and capped per element. Useful before deleting or moving something. Read-only.

ids.description: Element ids of the target document (1-50).

includeDependents.description: Also list dependent elements (what Revit deletes with it: tags, sketches, hosted elements...). Default false.

dependentCategories.description: Only dependents of these categories (any language). Default: all with a category.

dependentsLimit.description: Most dependents listed per element, 1-1000 (default 100); the count stays exact.

tools.name: get_element_rooms
tools.description: Which room each element is in, for a phase (default: the last phase). Family instances use Revit's Room, From Room and To Room (doors/windows: the two sides; null = exterior). Other elements fall back to the room at their location point, curve midpoint or bounding-box centre (method reported, with a warning). Optionally returns the MEP space too. Read-only.

ids.description: Element ids (doors, windows, furniture, equipment, any placed element), 1-500.

phase.description: Phase to evaluate rooms in (name or id). Default: the project's last phase.

includeSpaces.description: Also return the MEP space containing the element (default false).

tools.name: get_family_instances
tools.description: List the instances of a loadable family or of one type: id, type, level, host (id and category), location in mm (point + rotation in degrees, or curve ends), facing/hand flipped, group membership and optional extra parameter fields; filter by view and level; paged with an exact total. Read-only.

type.description: One type: id, "Family: Type" or type name.

view.description: Only instances visible in this view (name or id).

level.description: Only instances on this level (name or id).

fields.description: Extra parameters to return per instance ({guid} | {builtIn} | {name}, instance then type), in wire units.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

tools.name: get_link_elements
tools.description: Read elements inside a loaded Revit link (read-only): id, reference "linkInstanceId:elementId" (usable by get_element_details / get_element_parameters), name, category, family/type, level, location and bounding box in mm (in host coordinates by default, using the link's total transform) and the requested fields. Ids belong to the linked document. Links are never write targets: open the source RVT to edit it. Paged with total. Read-only.

link.description: The Revit link instance: its id, or its file / type name ("Structure.rvt" or "Structure").

categories.description: Categories to read inside the link, any language: OST_Walls / Walls / Paredes (at least one).

fields.description: Parameters to return for each element (wire units), each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

coordinates.description: host (default): locations and boxes transformed into the host model; link: the link's own coordinates.

tools.name: get_model_health
tools.description: Model check-up: score 0-100 and grade A-F from warnings, imported (not linked) CAD, in-place families, model groups, views not on sheets, detail lines, unplaced/unenclosed rooms, file size and (deep: true) purgeable families/types. Returns every metric, the penalty it cost and prioritized findings with the fix and the tool to use next (get_model_warnings, purge_unused, audit_sheets_views, audit_families...). Read-only.

deep.description: Also count purgeable families/types (slower on big models). Default false.

topN.description: How many top warning types to show, 0-20 (default 5).

tools.name: get_model_warnings
tools.description: Summarize the model's warnings (Review Warnings) grouped by warning type - the language-neutral FailureDefinitionId, so pt-BR and English texts group the same - or by category. Each group has count, distinct elements, the text in Revit's language, example element ids and, for common types, a suggested fix. Largest groups first, paged. Read-only.

groupBy.description: definition (default): one group per warning type (FailureDefinitionId, language-neutral); category: by the category of the first failing element.

categories.description: Only warnings involving elements of these categories (any language: OST_Walls / Walls / Paredes).

maxExamplesPerGroup.description: Example warnings (with element ids) per group, 0-50 (default 5).

limit.description: Groups per page, 1-500 (default 50), largest groups first.

tools.name: get_project_coordinates
tools.description: The model's coordinate systems: internal origin, Project Base Point and Survey Point (position in internal coordinates in mm, their shared values N/S, E/W, elevation in mm, angle to true north in degrees, clipped flag), the active shared location (offset and rotation of the internal origin in shared coordinates), named locations, and site latitude/longitude. Every tool works in internal coordinates in mm; use this to convert. With link: that link's transform into the host (origin mm, rotation deg). Read-only.

link.description: Optional Revit link (id or name): also return its transform into the host.

tools.name: get_project_info
tools.description: Project and document metadata: title, path, central model, worksharing, Revit version, Project Information fields (name, number, client, address, status, issue date, author, organization, building name; read by built-in parameter, so it works in any Revit language) and the active view. Ask for more with include[]: phases, worksets, levels (elevation mm), links, counts (elements per main category), units (display units) and parameters (every Project Information parameter in wire units). Read-only.

include.description: Extra sections: phases, worksets, levels, links, counts, units, parameters (all Project Information parameters). Default: only the metadata.

tools.name: get_room_boundaries
tools.description: Boundary loops of rooms, areas or MEP spaces: for each loop its segments (curve type, start/end and midpoint in mm, length mm) and the bounding element (wall, room separation line, column...; linkInstanceId + linkedElementId when the element is inside a Revit link). The first loop is the outer one, the others are holes. boundaryLocation picks the wall face (finish, center, core). Unplaced or unenclosed rooms return no loops and their status. Read-only.

boundaryLocation.description: Which wall face bounds a room/space: finish (default), center, coreCenter or coreBoundary. Areas ignore it.

includeBoundaryElements.description: Return the bounding element of each segment (id, category, link) (default true).

tools.name: get_room_openings
tools.description: Doors and windows of each room, resolved per phase with Revit's From Room / To Room (not by geometry): for each opening its id, category, family/type, mark, width/height in mm, host wall, side (from/to), the room on the other side (null = exterior), phase status (New, Existing, Demolished, Temporary) and optional orientation and parameters. By default each room is evaluated in its own phase; pass phase to force one. Openings hosted in linked walls are not seen. Paged by room. Read-only.

roomIds.description: Rooms by id. Combine with roomNumbers / level, or omit all three for every placed room.

level.description: Only rooms on this level (name or id).

categories.description: doors, windows or both (default both).

phase.description: Phase used for From/To Room and to decide which openings exist (name or id). Default: each room's own phase.

parameters.description: Extra parameters to read on each opening (instance, then type), each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

includeOrientation.description: Return facing/hand orientation vectors and flips (default true).

tools.name: get_schedulable_fields
tools.description: List the fields that can be added to a schedule: name (Revit's language), fieldType (Instance, ElementType, Count, Room, Material...), parameterId, builtIn and guid, so create_schedule and modify_schedule_fields can reference them language-neutrally. Works for an existing schedule or for a category + kind not scheduled yet (probed with a temporary schedule that is always rolled back; nothing is changed). Read-only.

schedule.description: Existing schedule (name or id). Give this, or category (+ kind) for a schedule not created yet.

category.description: Category of a schedule not created yet, in any language (OST_Rooms, Rooms, Ambientes). Not needed for sheet_list/view_list.

kind.description: Kind of the schedule to probe when using category (default regular).

nameContains.description: Only fields whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

tools.name: get_schedule_data
tools.description: Read what a schedule shows: the visible columns and the rows as Revit renders them (cell text with the project's formatting and units, calculated values included; hidden fields are left out). Group headers/footers and the grand total come as ordinary rows, in table order. Paged with limit/offset over the body rows; use export_schedule for a CSV file. Read-only.

includeHeadings.description: Also return the heading rows (column headings and heading groups) as Revit draws them. Default false: columns[] already names each column.

skipBlankRows.description: Leave out blank separator rows (default true).

tools.name: get_schedule_definition
tools.description: Full definition of a schedule: kind, category, fields in order (name, heading, fieldType, builtIn/guid, hidden, calculated/combined, width in mm, alignment, totals), filters (op and value in wire units), sorting/grouping (order, header, footer, blank line), itemization, grand totals and title/headers/grid-line flags. Formulas of calculated fields are not readable through the Revit API. Read-only.

tools.name: get_session_changes
tools.description: What changed in the target document during this session: net created / modified / deleted elements (id, UniqueId, name, category, transaction names, by MCP or by the user), the last created element still in the model, and lastSeq to ask again for only newer changes (sinceSeq). Tracking starts at the first call of this tool in the Revit session (earlier changes are unknown: the first call returns trackingStarted=true). Undo/redo is included. Filter by time, categories or onlyByMcp; paged. operation=reset starts a new baseline. Does not change the model.

operation.description: get (default): report changes; reset: forget what was recorded for this document and start a new baseline.

sinceSeq.description: Only events after this sequence number (lastSeq of a previous call). Default: since tracking started.

since.description: Only events after this ISO-8601 time (e.g. 2026-10-17T14:00:00Z).

categories.description: Only elements of these categories (any language).

onlyByMcp.description: Only changes made by this MCP's framework tools (transactions named "MCP: ..."), default false.

includeModified.description: Include modified elements (default true; modifications are often numerous).

tools.name: get_session_context
tools.description: Call first. Returns this Revit session's state: add-in version and capabilityHash (compare with the server's manifest to detect an outdated add-in), Revit version/build/language, every open document (docId, title, isFamilyDocument, isWorkshared, isActive, isReadOnly, isModified), the active document, the targeted document, the active view and the number of queued tool calls.

tools.name: get_sheet_layout
tools.description: Layout of one sheet in paper mm (sheet coordinates, the same ones place_on_sheet and create_sheets use): title block with its extents and paper size, each viewport with view, scale, box centre, box outline, label outline, rotation, viewport type, detail number and title on sheet, and each schedule instance with its insertion point and extents. Optionally sheet and title block parameters. Read-only.

includeParameters.description: Include the sheet's and title block's parameters (compact; default false).

tools.name: get_titleblock_parameters
tools.description: Read the parameters that fill a title block: the sheet's own parameters (number, name, drawn by, dates...) and the title block family instance's (and optionally type's), with values in wire units and the 'on' owner (sheet / titleblock / titleblock_type) to use in set_titleblock_parameters. Filter by parameters[]; paged by sheet. Read-only.

sheets.description: Sheets (numbers, names or ids). Omit for every non-placeholder sheet (paged).

target.description: Where to read: both (sheet + title block instance, default), sheet, titleblock (instance), titleblock_type, or all.

parameters.description: Only these parameters, each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}. Omit for all.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

tools.name: get_view_image
tools.description: Render one view or sheet, by id, to a PNG (or JPG) and return it as an image the assistant can look at (data.image), sized by pixels/fitDirection. Optionally keep the file in an allowed folder (saveTo). Schedules can't be rendered. Read-only: the model is not changed.

viewId.description: Id of the view or sheet to render (any document view; it does not need to be open).

pixels.description: Image size in pixels along fitDirection, 64-4096 (default 1600). Big images cost many tokens.

fitDirection.description: Which side 'pixels' applies to: horizontal (default) or vertical.

returnImage.description: Return the image so the assistant can see it (default true). false only saves the file (needs saveTo).

saveTo.description: Optional folder to keep the image in (absolute inside an allowed root, or relative to Documents\RevitMCP\exports).

tools.name: get_view_visibility
tools.description: Visibility/Graphics state of a view or template: hidden and overridden categories (BuiltInCategory + local name, paged), applied filters with visibility, enabled flag and overrides, the view template and which V/G parts it controls, discipline, phase, detail level, temporary hide/isolate. Use before set_category_visibility / apply_view_filter. Read-only.

view.description: View or view template (name or id).

onlyChanged.description: true (default): list only hidden or overridden categories. false: every category that can be hidden.

includeOverrides.description: Include the override details of categories and filters (default true).

tools.name: import_parameters_table
tools.description: Import a CSV table (as written by export_parameters_table and edited in Excel) into parameters. Rows are found by the key column (UniqueId or ElementId); headers name the parameter ("Width [mm]", optional {builtIn:X}/{guid:G}); columns starting with '_' are ignored. ALWAYS run it first with dryRun:true (no approval needed): you get a per-cell diff (changed, unchanged, invalid, read-only, missing element/parameter) and nothing is kept. Then run it for real (needs approval): one transaction, read-back, atomic by default. Only reads inside the allowed folders. Undo: Ctrl+Z or send revert[] to set_parameters / set_type_parameters.

path.description: CSV file to read: absolute, or relative to Documents\RevitMCP\exports. Must be inside the allowed folders.

keyColumn.description: Header of the column that identifies the element (UniqueId or ElementId values). Default: the column named UniqueId or ElementId, else the first one.

columns.description: Only import these parameter columns (header names without the [unit] / {ref} suffix). Default: every column not starting with '_'.

decimalSeparator.description: Decimal separator used in the file: "," (default, as exported) or ".".

emptyCellsClear.description: true: an empty cell clears the parameter. false (default): empty cells are ignored.

target.description: Where to resolve each column: auto (default: instance, then type), instance or type.

maxWrites.description: Refuse when more cells would be written (default 5000, max 20000).

sampleSize.description: How many changed cells to list (default 50).

atomic.description: true (default): any problem cell (invalid value, read-only, missing element or parameter) or failed write rolls everything back. false: write the valid cells and report the rest.

allowCritical.description: Allow critical parameters (type, level, phase, workset, host; repeated Mark). Default false.

tools.name: list_category_parameters
tools.description: List the parameters found on elements of a category (any language: OST_Doors, Doors, Portas), instance and/or type, so you can pick the exact reference before reading or writing. Each entry has name, builtIn, guid, storageType, dataType, group, readOnly, on (instance/type), how many sampled elements have it (seenOn) and a value (filledCount), and optionally distinct values. Inspects a sample (sampleSize) of the category. Read-only.

category.description: Category in any language: OST_Walls, Walls or Paredes.

sampleSize.description: How many elements (and types) to inspect, from the lowest ids (default 200, max 5000). Parameters can differ between families of one category.

withDistinctValues.description: Return up to this many distinct values per parameter (default 0 = none, max 20).

nameFilter.description: Only parameters whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

editableOnly.description: Leave out read-only parameters. Default false.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List the tools the installed Revit add-in provides, with kind (read/write/ui), risk, toolset, whether it changes the model, whether it needs the user's approval (risk medium or high), batchable, idempotent and timeout. Filter by text, kind or toolset. Works with no document open.

contains.description: Only tools whose name or description contains this text (case and accents ignored).

kind.description: Only tools of this kind: read, write or ui.

toolset.description: Only tools of this toolset (core, query, parameters, sheets, export, qa, documents, ...).

includeDescriptions.description: Include each tool's full description (default false: first sentence only).

tools.name: list_families
tools.description: List the loadable and in-place families of the model: id, name, category, in-place and editable flags, type count, placed instance count, optionally each type (id, name, instance count). Filter by name text, categories (any language), in-place, or onlyUnused (purge candidates). System families (walls, floors, roofs...) are not Family elements: use get_available_family_types or find_elements with elementKind=types for those. Ordered by category then name, paged. Read-only.

nameContains.description: Only families whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

categories.description: Only families of these categories (any language: OST_Doors / Doors / Portas).

includeTypes.description: List the types of each family (default false).

includeInstanceCount.description: Count placed instances per family (and per type when includeTypes) (default true).

onlyUnused.description: Only families without any placed instance (default false).

inPlace.description: false = only loadable families, true = only in-place families, any (default).

tools.name: list_levels
tools.description: List the levels ordered by elevation: id, name, elevation in mm relative to the internal origin (elevationMm), the elevation Revit displays (displayedElevationMm, relative to the Project Base Point or Survey Point according to the level type's Elevation Base), building story flag, and the floor/ceiling plan views associated with it. Optionally counts the elements on each level. Read-only.

includeElementCounts.description: Also count the model elements associated with each level (slower on big models; default false).

tools.name: list_links
tools.description: List the Revit links (type id, name, path, loaded/unloaded/not found, attachment or overlay, nested, instance count) and the CAD files (linked vs imported, path, status, instances and the view owning view-specific ones). Use the linkTypeId with manage_links to reload or unload. Read-only.

kind.description: rvt (Revit links), cad (linked and imported DWG/DXF/DGN/SKP...) or all (default).

tools.name: list_materials
tools.description: List the project's materials with class, shading color (#RRGGBB), transparency, surface and cut patterns with their colors, render appearance asset and, optionally, how many elements use each. Filter by name or class; sorted by name; paged with an exact total. Read-only.

nameContains.description: Only materials whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

materialClass.description: Only this material class (e.g. Concrete / Concreto, Paint / Pintura), case and accents ignored.

includeUseCount.description: Count the model elements that use each material (slower on big models). Default false.

tools.name: list_parameter_bindings
tools.description: List the project and shared parameters bound in the document: name, guid (shared), isShared, bindingKind (instance/type), dataType, group, variesAcrossGroups and the bound categories (localized name plus OST_ name). Filter by name, guid, kind or category; paged. Use before bind_shared_parameter to see what is already bound. Read-only.

nameFilter.description: Only parameters whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

guid.description: Only the shared parameter with this GUID.

kind.description: all (default), shared (shared parameters bound to the project) or project (project-only parameters).

category.description: Only bindings that include this category (any language).

includeCategories.description: List the bound categories of each parameter (default true).

tools.name: list_phases
tools.description: List the project phases in chronological order (id, name, order; the last one is where new work normally goes) and the phase filters with the presentation of each phase status (New, Existing, Demolished, Temporary: ShowByCategory, ShowOverriden or DontShow). Phase names are translated by Revit ("Existing" / "Existente"): pass ids to other tools when in doubt. Read-only.

includePhaseFilters.description: Also list the phase filters and how each shows New/Existing/Demolished/Temporary elements (default true).

tools.name: list_recent_models
tools.description: List the models Revit opened recently (its MRU list in Revit.ini), most recent first, with path, whether the file still exists, last modified time and size. Works with no document open. Use it to find a model to open. Read-only.

revitVersion.description: Revit version whose recent list to read, e.g. "2025". Default: the running Revit.

tools.name: list_revisions
tools.description: List revisions in sequence order: id, sequence, number, description, date, issued by/to, issued flag, visibility and numbering sequence; with includeSheets the sheets that carry each revision (manual vs from clouds); with includeSequences the numbering sequences. Paged. Read-only.

includeSheets.description: List the sheets each revision is on, and whether it comes from clouds or was added manually (default true).

includeSequences.description: Also list the revision numbering sequences (default false).

tools.name: list_saved_selections
tools.description: List the saved selections of the model (Manage > Saved Selections, stored as selection filters): id, name, element count (elements that still exist) and optionally their ids. Select one in the UI with select_elements {savedSelection}; create with save_selection; delete with delete_saved_selection. Read-only.

nameContains.description: Only names containing this text (case and accents ignored).

includeIds.description: Return the element ids of each saved selection (up to idsLimit each; default false).

idsLimit.description: Most ids returned per saved selection, 1-5000 (default 500).

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List the schedules of the document (regular, material takeoff, key, sheet/view lists, note blocks) with id, name, kind, category, field count and the sheets they are placed on. Internal title-block revision schedules and schedule templates are excluded. Filter by kind, category (any language) or name; paged with limit/offset. Read-only.

category.description: Only schedules of this category, in any language (OST_Doors, Doors, Portas).

nameContains.description: Only schedules whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

includePlacement.description: List the sheets each schedule is placed on (default true).

tools.name: list_sheets
tools.description: List sheets in natural number order (A-2 before A-10): id, number, name, placeholder flag, title block, current revision, viewport and schedule counts; optionally the viewports/schedules (includeViewports) and revisions (includeRevisions). Filter by numberContains / nameContains; paged with limit/offset. Read-only.

numberContains.description: Only sheets whose number contains this text (e.g. "A-1").

nameContains.description: Only sheets whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

includeViewports.description: List each sheet's viewports and schedules (default false: counts only).

tools.name: list_spatial_elements
tools.description: List rooms, areas or MEP spaces with number, name, level, phase, area scheme, area (m2), perimeter (mm), volume (m3; 0 unless volume computation is on) and status: placed, notPlaced (deleted from plan but still in schedules), notEnclosed (placed but not bounded, area 0) or redundant (placed in a region another one already occupies). Filter by level, phase, area scheme, status, name/number text. Ordered by level then number, paged with total. Read-only.

level.description: Only on this level (name or id).

phase.description: Only rooms/spaces of this phase (name or id). Areas have no phase.

areaScheme.description: Only areas of this area scheme (name or id), e.g. Gross Building / Rentable.

status.description: Only these statuses: placed, notPlaced, notEnclosed, redundant. Default: all.

nameContains.description: Only names containing this text (case and accents ignored).

fields.description: Extra parameters to return for each item (wire units), each {guid} | {builtIn} | {name}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

tools.name: list_titleblocks
tools.description: List title block types ("Family: Type" as create_sheets expects) with id, whether it is the document default, paper size in mm when the family exposes it, and how many sheets use it (with up to 20 sheet numbers). Filter by nameContains, skip unused types with includeUnused:false; paged. Read-only.

nameContains.description: Only title blocks whose "Family: Type" contains this text (case and accents ignored).

includeUnused.description: Include types not used by any sheet (default true).

tools.name: list_view_templates
tools.description: List view templates with id, name, view type, scale, detail level, how many views use them (includeUsage) and optionally the parameters each one controls (includeControlled). Filter by viewType (FloorPlan, Section, ThreeD...) and nameContains; paged with limit/offset. Read-only.

viewType.description: Only templates for this view type, e.g. FloorPlan, CeilingPlan, Section, Elevation, ThreeD, DraftingView, Schedule.

nameContains.description: Only templates whose name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

includeUsage.description: Count the views that use each template (default true).

includeControlled.description: List the parameters each template controls (default false).

tools.name: list_views
tools.description: List views, schedules, legends, sheets and view templates with filters (viewTypes, isTemplate, nameContains, onSheet, level). Each item: id, name, viewType, isTemplate, level, scale, detail level, discipline, phase, view template applied, and the sheet(s) where it is placed. Internal views (project/system browser, revision schedules of title blocks) are excluded. Optionally lists the view family types. Ordered by type then name, paged with total. Read-only.

viewTypes.description: Only these Revit view types, e.g. FloorPlan, CeilingPlan, Elevation, Section, ThreeD, DraftingView, Legend, Schedule, DrawingSheet, AreaPlan, Detail, EngineeringPlan.

isTemplate.description: false = only views (default), true = only view templates, any = both.

nameContains.description: Only names containing this text (case and accents ignored).

onSheet.description: true = only views placed on a sheet, false = only views not placed, any (default).

level.description: Only plan views of this level (name or id).

includeViewFamilyTypes.description: Also return the view family types (used to create views), default false.

tools.name: list_worksets
tools.description: List the worksets of a workshared model: id, name, kind, whether it is the active workset, open, editable by this user, owner, default visibility, optionally element counts. A model without worksharing returns isWorkshared=false and an empty list (not an error). Read-only.

includeSystem.description: Also list system worksets (families, standards, views), default false.

includeElementCounts.description: Count the elements in each user workset (slow on big models; default false).

tools.name: load_family
tools.description: Load (or reload with overwrite) a family .rfa into the project, only from the allowed folders (Documents\RevitMCP by default, plus REVIT_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS). Optionally load only some types. Returns the family id, category and its types with ids; an already-loaded family is reported, not duplicated. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

path.description: The .rfa file: absolute, or relative to Documents\RevitMCP\families. Must be inside the allowed folders (REVIT_MCP_ALLOWED_DIRS adds the office library).

overwrite.description: If the family is already loaded, reload it from the file. Default false (report it as already loaded).

overwriteParameterValues.description: When reloading, also overwrite the parameter values of existing types. Default false.

types.description: Load only these types (names as in the family). Default: all types.

tools.name: manage_links
tools.description: Reload or unload Revit links by link type id (from list_links). Reload re-reads the file from its saved path (fails with the reason if the file is missing); unload removes the link's geometry from the session until reloaded. Neither can be undone with Ctrl+Z: undo an unload with reload. dryRun lists what would happen. CAD links are listed by list_links but not managed here.

operation.description: reload (reload from the saved path) or unload.

linkTypeIds.description: Revit link type ids (linkTypeId from list_links).

tools.name: manage_view_templates
tools.description: Manage view templates: create_from_view (sourceView + newName), duplicate (template + newName), rename, delete (detaches the views that use it; refused above maxUsedByViews, default 0) and set_controlled (which parameters the template controls, by dialog name or BuiltInParameter). Results are read back (ids, names, controlled list). Needs approval. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

operation.description: create_from_view, duplicate, rename, delete or set_controlled.

template.description: Existing template (name or id), for duplicate, rename, delete and set_controlled.

sourceView.description: View (name or id) whose settings become a new template, for create_from_view.

newName.description: Name of the new template (create_from_view, duplicate) or the new name (rename). Must be free among templates.

controlled.description: set_controlled: parameters the template must control (names as in the View Template dialog, or BuiltInParameter names).

uncontrolled.description: set_controlled: parameters the template must stop controlling.

maxUsedByViews.description: delete: refuse when more than this many views use the template (default 0: only unused templates). Views that use it are detached first.

tools.name: modify_element
tools.description: Several edits on ONE element in a single transaction (one Ctrl+Z), in this order: flips (facing, hand, work plane), instance parameter writes (set_parameters rules, read back), move (mm), rotate about the vertical axis through the element (degrees), then pin/unpin. A pinned element is unpinned for the move/rotate when pinned:false is given. Everything is rolled back if any step fails. Returns what was applied, the read-back location and revert[] for the parameters. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

elementId.description: The element to edit (id or UniqueId).

parameters.description: Instance parameter values to write (same rules as set_parameters; type parameters are refused).

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: New value (wire units mm, m2, m3, deg, %; ElementId parameters by id or name; null clears text).

unit.description: Optional unit override for a number (m, cm, mm, ft, in, deg, rad, %, internal...).

x.description: X coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

y.description: Y coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

z.description: Z coordinate (project internal origin). Unit: mm.

rotate.description: Rotation about the vertical axis through the element's location point (or bounding-box centre). Unit: deg.

flipFacing.description: Flip the facing orientation (doors, windows, families that allow it).

flipHand.description: Flip the hand orientation (doors, windows, families that allow it).

flipWorkPlane.description: Flip a work-plane-based family to the other side of its work plane.

pinned.description: Pin (true) or unpin (false) after the other edits.

allowCritical.description: Allow critical parameters (level, phase, workset, host...). Default false.

tools.name: modify_schedule_fields
tools.description: Edit the columns of a schedule with ordered operations: add a schedulable field (builtIn/guid/name, optional index), remove, move to an index, or update heading, hidden, width (mm), alignment and totals. All operations succeed or none is applied; unknown fields fail with suggestions instead of being ignored. Calculated fields cannot be created via the API. Returns the fields read back. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

operations.description: Operations applied in order, all or nothing (up to 100).

op.description: add (a schedulable field), remove, move (to index) or update (heading, hidden, width, alignment, totals).

field.description: add: {builtIn}/{guid}/{name} of a schedulable field (see get_schedulable_fields). Others: {name: column heading or field name} | {builtIn} | {guid} of a field in the schedule.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

fieldType.description: add only: disambiguates fields with the same parameter (Instance, ElementType/type, Room, Material...).

index.description: add/move: 0-based position among all fields (hidden included). add without index appends.

widthMm.description: Column width on the sheet (paper size). Unit: mm.

total.description: Show totals for the column (numeric fields only).

tools.name: place_door_window
tools.description: Place doors or windows in a wall, at a distance along the wall (mm from its start to the opening centre) or at a point projected onto it, with optional sill height (mm). Before placing, checks that the opening fits in the wall's clear length (corners deducted) and does not overlap other openings, and refuses with the numbers in mm. Curtain walls are refused. Read-back: host, sill, head, position. One Ctrl+Z undoes the call.

familyType.description: Door or window type as "Family: Type", type name or id. An ambiguous name returns placed:false with candidates.

alongWall.description: Distance in mm from the wall's start point to the centre of the opening. Give alongWall or point.

point.description: Plan point in mm near the wall; it is projected onto the wall's location line. Give alongWall or point.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

sillHeight.description: Sill height in mm above the level (windows; doors usually 0). Omit to keep the family's default.

level.description: Level by name or id. Default: the wall's base level.

flipFacing.description: Flip to open to the other side of the wall. Default false.

flipHand.description: Swap the hinge side. Default false.

allowOverlap.description: Skip the overlap check against other doors/windows in the wall. Default false.

parameters.description: Instance parameters to set after placing, by name (e.g. {"Marca": "P01"}).

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back the whole call. true: failed items are skipped and listed in failed[].

tools.name: place_family_instance
tools.description: Place family instances (furniture, fixtures, lights, equipment, plants, generic models): free on a level with offset, hosted on a wall/floor/ceiling, on a face of a host (e.g. lights under a ceiling), or along a line for line-based families. Coordinates in mm, rotation in degrees. The type must be named; an ambiguous name returns placed:false with candidates. Instance parameters can be set on creation. Returns ids and read-back location/level/host. One Ctrl+Z undoes the call.

familyType.description: Family type as "Family: Type", type name or id. An ambiguous name returns placed:false with the candidates.

category.description: Category to narrow the type search (e.g. "Mobiliário", "Furniture", "OST_LightingFixtures").

placement.description: auto (default) follows the family: point = free on a level; host = wall/floor/ceiling-hosted family; face = on a face of hostId (face-based or work-plane families, e.g. lights on a ceiling); line = line-based family from location to end.

location.description: Insertion point in mm (start point for line placement). z is only used to pick a face.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

z.description: Z in mm. For level-based placement it is ignored (use offset); for face placement it helps pick the face.

end.description: End point in mm for line placement.

x.description: X coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

y.description: Y coordinate in mm from the project's internal origin.

z.description: Z in mm. For level-based placement it is ignored (use offset); for face placement it helps pick the face.

level.description: Level by name or id. Required for point/line placement; for hosted placement defaults to the host's level.

offset.description: Elevation from the level in mm (e.g. 2100 for a wall-mounted item). Default 0. Not used for face placement.

hostId.description: Host element id (wall, floor, ceiling, roof or any element with faces) for host/face placement.

faceSide.description: face placement: which face of the host. auto = bottom of ceilings, top of floors/roofs, the nearest side of walls.

rotation.description: Rotation around the vertical axis in degrees, counter-clockwise. Default 0. Ignored for wall-hosted placement.

flipFacing.description: Flip the facing orientation after placing. Default false.

flipHand.description: Flip the hand orientation after placing. Default false.

parameters.description: Instance parameters to set after placing, by name, e.g. {"Marca": "M01"}; same value rules as set_parameters.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back the whole call. true: failed items are skipped and listed in failed[]. Ambiguous types never abort: they come back as placed:false.

tools.name: place_on_sheet
tools.description: Place views and legends (as viewports) and schedules (as schedule instances) on sheets at x/y in paper mm, anchored by center, top_left or bottom_left of the placed box, with an optional viewport type. Checks Viewport.CanAddViewToSheet (a view can be on one sheet only; legends and schedules on many). Final positions are read back. Undo: Ctrl+Z or delete the returned ids.

view.description: View, legend or schedule to place (name or id).

x.description: X of the anchor point on the sheet, paper mm (sheet coordinates).

y.description: Y of the anchor point on the sheet, paper mm (sheet coordinates).

anchor.description: Which point of the placed box lands on x/y: center (default for views), top_left (default for schedules) or bottom_left.

viewportType.description: Viewport type name or id (views only), e.g. a type without title.

continueOnError.description: false (default): any failure rolls back every placement. true: failed ones are listed in failed[].

tools.name: purge_unused
tools.description: Find and (with apply: true) delete unused families, types, materials and patterns - the same list as Revit's Purge Unused on 2024+ (older versions: families and types only). By default it only lists (apply false); dryRun: true previews the exact deletions with real ids. exclude[] protects names by regex. Repeats up to 'passes' times to catch cascades. Undo: Ctrl+Z (one transaction).

targets.description: What to purge (default families, types, materials): families, types, materials, fillPatterns, linePatterns, viewTemplates, other.

apply.description: false (default): only list what is unused (nothing is deleted). true: delete it (one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole purge).

exclude.description: Regular expressions on the element name; matching elements are never purged (e.g. "^Carimbo", "_PADRAO$").

maxElements.description: Delete at most this many elements in one call, 1-10000 (default 2000).

passes.description: apply only: repeat the purge up to this many times, 1-5 (default 3), since deleting a family can free its nested families and materials.

listLimit.description: Maximum items listed in the result, 0-2000 (default 300); counts are always complete.

tools.name: rename_elements
tools.description: Rename many elements at once: views, sheets (name or number), levels, grids, rooms (Name parameter), types, families, materials. Operations: set (with {n} counter), prefix, suffix, findReplace, regexReplace. Before writing it checks characters Revit forbids and collisions in the scope Revit uses (inside the batch and against the document); swapped names go through a temporary pass. Every name is read back. ALWAYS preview with dryRun:true first (no approval; returns the before/after table), then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z.

elementIds.description: Elements to rename (views, sheets, levels, grids, rooms, types, families, materials...). Alternative to categories.

categories.description: Categories in any language (OST_Views, OST_Sheets, Levels, Ambientes...): every element (or type, with elementKind) of them.

nameContains.description: Only elements whose current name contains this text (case and accents ignored).

operation.description: set (value; "{n}" becomes a counter), prefix / suffix (value), findReplace (find → replace), regexReplace (.NET regex, replace may use $1).

value.description: New name (set) or the text to add (prefix / suffix). "{n}" is replaced by a counter.

find.description: Text or regular expression to look for (findReplace / regexReplace).

replace.description: Replacement (default empty). "{n}" is replaced by a counter.

separator.description: Text between the name and the prefix/suffix (default none).

ignoreCase.description: findReplace / regexReplace ignore case. Default false.

sheetField.description: For sheets: rename the name (default) or the number.

atomic.description: true (default): any invalid name or collision renames nothing. false: rename the valid ones and report the rest.

tools.name: rename_types
tools.description: Rename types in batch (or, with renameFamilies, their loadable families): set with {n} counter, prefix, suffix, findReplace or regexReplace, over explicit type ids or every type of categories filtered by family and name. Checks forbidden characters and collisions within each family before writing, handles swapped names, reads names back and reports instancesAffected. System families (walls, floors) can't be renamed, only their types. Preview with dryRun:true (no approval), then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z.

typeIds.description: Types to rename (ids as strings; an instance id means its type). Alternative to categories.

categories.description: Every type of these categories (any language), narrowed by familyName / nameContains.

familyName.description: Only types of this family (case and accents ignored).

nameContains.description: Only types (or families) whose current name contains this text.

renameFamilies.description: Rename the loadable families of the selected types instead of the types. Default false.

operation.description: set (value; "{n}" becomes a counter), prefix / suffix (value), findReplace (find → replace), regexReplace (.NET regex).

value.description: New name (set) or text to add (prefix / suffix).

find.description: Text or regular expression to look for.

separator.description: Text between the name and the prefix/suffix (default none).

ignoreCase.description: findReplace / regexReplace ignore case. Default false.

atomic.description: true (default): any invalid name or collision renames nothing.

tools.name: renumber_elements
tools.description: Renumber rooms, doors, windows, parking spaces or any element with a text number/Mark: by position (rows top-to-bottom then left-to-right, or columns), by current value or by id; start, increment, zero padding, prefix/suffix ({level} = level name) and optional restart per level. Writes in two passes (temporary unique values first) so swapping numbers never collides; warns when a new number already exists on another element of the category. Preview with dryRun:true (no approval), then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z or send revert[] to set_parameters.

elementIds.description: Elements to renumber. Alternative to categories / useSelection.

categories.description: Categories in any language (OST_Rooms, Doors, Janelas...). Narrow with view and level.

view.description: Only elements visible in this view (name or id).

level.description: Only elements on this level (name or id).

useSelection.description: Renumber Revit's current selection (target must be the active document). Default false.

parameter.description: Text parameter that holds the number. Default: Number for rooms/spaces, Mark for everything else.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

prefix.description: Text before the number; {level} is replaced by the element's level name (e.g. "P-{level}-").

sortBy.description: Order: yThenX (rows top to bottom, left to right; default), xThenY (columns left to right, top to bottom), current (natural order of the current values), id.

rowTolerance.description: Elements whose Y (or X for xThenY) differ by less than this are in the same row (default 500). Unit: mm.

perLevel.description: Restart numbering on each level (levels by elevation). Default false.

allowDuplicates.description: Allow the new numbers to repeat (e.g. perLevel without {level} in the prefix). Default false.

tools.name: renumber_sheets
tools.description: Renumber and/or rename sheets in bulk by explicit items, findReplace on numbers, or a sequence (prefix + zero-padded counter + suffix over an ordered list). The final numbering is computed first and checked for forbidden characters and collisions (with every other sheet, placeholders included); then numbers are applied in two passes via temporary numbers so swaps like A<->B work. Read back. Use dryRun to preview. Needs approval. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

items.description: Explicit changes: {sheet, newNumber?, newName?} per sheet, up to 1000.

find.description: Text to find in the sheet numbers (case-sensitive).

sheets.description: Only these sheets (numbers, names or ids). Omit for every sheet whose number contains find.

sequence.description: Number the given sheets in order: prefix + zero-padded counter + suffix.

sheets.description: Sheets in the order they get numbers (numbers, names or ids).

digits.description: Zero-pad the counter to this many digits (default 2: 01, 02...).

tools.name: replace_type_instances
tools.description: Replace every instance of one type with another type of the same category, in the whole project, in a view or in the selection. Types by id, "Family: Type" or name. Instances inside groups are skipped and reported (Revit can't change them without editing the group). Preview with dryRun:true (no approval; returns the count and ids), then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z, or run again with fromType/toType swapped on the returned ids via change_element_type.

fromType.description: Type to replace: id, "Family: Type" or type name.

toType.description: Replacement type: id, "Family: Type" or type name (same category).

category.description: Category (any language) to disambiguate type names.

scope.description: project (default), view (instances visible in view) or selection (selected instances only).

view.description: View name or id for scope=view.

tools.name: save_document
tools.description: Save the target document to its own file, or Save As a new file inside the allowed folders (saveAsPath). Workshared models are saved locally only: it never synchronizes with central (ask the user to sync in Revit), and Save As is refused for them. A never-saved document needs saveAsPath. Saving can't be undone; dryRun reports what would be saved.

saveAsPath.description: Save a copy under a new name (Save As): absolute inside an allowed root, or relative to Documents\RevitMCP\models. The document then points to the new file. Not allowed for workshared models.

overwrite.description: Save As only: replace an existing file (default false: fail with FILE_EXISTS).

compact.description: Compact the file while saving (slower, smaller). Default false.

tools.name: save_selection
tools.description: Save a named selection in the model (the same as Manage > Save Selection, synchronized to central with the model): the given element ids, or the current UI selection. With overwrite=true an existing saved selection of the same name gets the new elements. Returns its id and the element count read back. Undo with Ctrl+Z or delete_saved_selection. Supports dryRun.

name.description: Name of the saved selection.

elementIds.description: Elements to save, by id or UniqueId (strings). Default: the current UI selection (target must be the active document).

overwrite.description: Replace the elements of an existing saved selection with the same name (default false).

tools.name: select_elements
tools.description: Change the selection in Revit's UI (active document only): replace, add, remove or clear, with elements given by id/UniqueId, by a saved selection, or as everything visible in a view (optionally by category). Sources can be combined. Optionally zooms to the result. Does not change the model; elements inside links can't be selected this way. Returns the final selection count.

mode.description: replace (default) the selection, add to it, remove from it, or clear it.

elementIds.description: Elements by id or UniqueId (strings), max 5000.

savedSelection.description: Use the elements of this saved selection (name or id).

visibleInView.description: Use the elements visible in a view, optionally by category.

view.description: View name or id (default: the active view).

categories.description: Only these categories (any language). Default: every selectable element visible in the view.

zoom.description: Also zoom Revit to the resulting selection (default false).

tools.name: set_category_visibility
tools.description: Show/hide categories (and subcategories as "Category: Sub") and apply category graphic overrides (line colors/weight, surface/cut patterns and colors, transparency, halftone) in views or view templates. Categories by BuiltInCategory or name in any language. Views whose V/G is controlled by a template are refused with the template name (apply to the template instead). Read back per view. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

views.description: Views or view templates (names or ids), up to 200.

categories.description: Categories in any language (OST_Furniture, Furniture, Mobiliário); a subcategory as "Category: Subcategory".

hidden.description: true hides the categories, false shows them. Omit to leave visibility alone.

overrides.description: Graphic overrides to apply to the categories (only the given fields change).

surfaceColor.description: Surface foreground pattern color as "#RRGGBB" (needs a surfacePattern, e.g. "solid").

surfacePattern.description: Surface foreground fill pattern name or id; "solid" for the solid fill; "none" to clear.

cutPattern.description: Cut foreground fill pattern name or id; "solid" for the solid fill; "none" to clear.

clearOverrides.description: Reset the categories' overrides before applying overrides (default false).

atomic.description: true (default): any failure rolls the whole call back. false: failures are reported per view/category.

tools.name: set_compound_structure
tools.description: Edit the layers of a basic wall, floor, roof or ceiling type: full replacement (layers with function, material, thickness in mm, shell counts) or patch by index; variable and structural layer. By default the type is DUPLICATED first (newTypeName) and only elementId / assignTo are switched to the copy, so other instances keep their structure; inPlace:true edits the type itself. Revit's validity check runs before writing; the result is read back. Preview with dryRun:true (no approval), then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z.

type.description: Wall, floor, roof or ceiling type: id, "Family: Type" or type name.

elementId.description: Alternative: an element of the type. With the default duplicate behaviour this element is switched to the new type.

category.description: Category (any language) to disambiguate the type name.

inPlace.description: Edit the type itself (changes EVERY instance). Default false: duplicate the type first and edit the copy.

newTypeName.description: Name of the duplicated type. Default: the original name with " (2)" (first free).

assignTo.description: Elements to switch to the new (duplicated) type. Default: elementId when given.

layers.description: Full replacement of the layers, exterior/top first. Alternative to patch.

function.description: structure, substrate, insulation, finish1, finish2, membrane or structuralDeck.

material.description: Material name or id; omit or "byCategory" for <By Category>.

thickness.description: Layer thickness (0 only for membranes). Unit: mm.

exteriorShellLayers.description: With layers: how many layers are outside the core on the exterior/top side.

interiorShellLayers.description: With layers: how many layers are outside the core on the interior/bottom side.

patch.description: Changes to existing layers by index (function, material, thickness).

index.description: Layer index as returned by get_compound_structure.

material.description: New material, name or id ("byCategory" for <By Category>).

variableLayerIndex.description: Floors/roofs: layer whose thickness varies with shape editing; -1 clears it.

structuralMaterialIndex.description: Layer that gives the structural material.

tools.name: set_element_phase
tools.description: Set Phase Created and/or Phase Demolished of elements (renovation work) by phase name or id; phaseDemolished "none" clears demolition. Checks that demolition is not before creation and that each element accepts phases, reads both back and returns old/new phase per element. This is the dedicated tool for phases (set_parameters blocks them). Undo: Ctrl+Z, or call again with the returned old phases.

elementIds.description: Elements to change.

phaseCreated.description: Phase Created, by name (as in the project, e.g. "Existente", "Construção nova") or id.

phaseDemolished.description: Phase Demolished, by name or id; "none" clears it (element not demolished).

atomic.description: true (default): any element that can't take the phases rolls everything back. false: change the others and report the failures.

tools.name: set_elements_pinned
tools.description: Pins or unpins elements by id in the target document. Elements already in the requested state are reported as unchanged; ids that don't exist are reported as notFound. Undo with Ctrl+Z or by calling it again with the opposite value. Supports dryRun.

elementIds.description: Ids of the elements to pin or unpin.

pinned.description: true pins the elements (they can't be moved or deleted by accident); false unpins them.

tools.name: set_graphic_overrides
tools.description: Override graphics of elements and/or categories in one view: projection/cut lines (colour #RRGGBB, weight 1-16, pattern), surface/cut foreground and background patterns (colour, pattern or "solid", visible), transparency 0-100, halftone, and hide/unhide. Merges with the existing overrides by default (nothing given is reset). Category overrides fail with VIEW_CONTROLLED_BY_TEMPLATE when the view template controls them. Returns the overrides read back. Undo: Ctrl+Z or clear_graphic_overrides.

view.description: View (name or id) where the overrides apply.

elementIds.description: Elements to override (ids, up to 5000). Give elementIds and/or categories.

categories.description: Categories to override in the view, in any language (OST_Walls, Walls, Paredes).

overrides.description: Overrides to set. Only what is given changes (see merge).

pattern.description: Line pattern name or id ("Solid" for continuous).
Line pattern name or id ("Solid" for continuous).
Fill pattern name or id ("solid" for a solid fill, in any language).
Fill pattern name or id ("solid" for a solid fill, in any language).
Fill pattern name or id ("solid" for a solid fill, in any language).
Fill pattern name or id ("solid" for a solid fill, in any language).

merge.description: true (default): keep the current overrides and change only what is given. false: replace them entirely.

visible.description: Hide (false) or unhide (true) the elements/categories in the view.

tools.name: set_material_graphics
tools.description: Edit a material's graphics: class, shading color (#RRGGBB), transparency, shininess, smoothness, use-render-appearance, surface and cut foreground/background patterns and colors, and the render appearance color (generic diffuse; a shared appearance asset is duplicated first so other materials don't change). Affects every element that uses the material. Values are read back and the before/after state returned. Preview with dryRun:true, then run (needs approval). Undo: Ctrl+Z.

useRenderAppearance.description: Use the render appearance for shading.

surfaceForegroundPattern.description: Surface foreground fill pattern: name or id, "solid", "none"; prefix "model:" / "drafting:" if the name exists in both.

surfaceBackgroundPattern.description: Surface background fill pattern (name, id, "solid" or "none").

cutForegroundPattern.description: Cut foreground fill pattern (name, id, "solid" or "none").

cutBackgroundPattern.description: Cut background fill pattern (name, id, "solid" or "none").

appearanceColor.description: Render appearance color "#RRGGBB" (generic diffuse). Edits the appearance asset; a shared asset is duplicated first.

material.description: Material to edit: name or id.

tools.name: set_parameters
tools.description: Write instance parameter values on 1..500 elements in one transaction (one Ctrl+Z). Reference parameters by guid, builtIn or name; numbers in wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %), ElementId parameters by id or name. Every write is read back: values Revit changed (formulas, rounding) come back as 'mismatch'. Atomic by default. Critical parameters (type, level, phase, workset, host) are blocked unless allowCritical. Type parameters are refused here: use set_type_parameters. Undo: Ctrl+Z, or send the returned revert[] back to this tool.

items.description: Writes to apply: one {elementId, parameter, value, unit?} per value. Up to 500 per call.

elementId.description: Element id or UniqueId, as a string.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: New value. Numbers in wire units (length mm, area m2, volume m3, angle deg, slope %); yes/no as true/false; ElementId parameters take an id or a name (level, phase, material, type); null clears text and ElementId values.

unit.description: Optional unit for this number instead of the wire default: m, cm, mm, ft, in, m2, ft2, m3, l, deg, rad, %, ratio, or internal (raw Revit value).

elementIds.description: Shortcut for the same value on several elements: element ids (strings), used with parameter + value instead of items.

parameter.description: Shortcut: the parameter to write on every element of elementIds.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: Shortcut: the value to write on every element of elementIds (same rules as items[].value).

unit.description: Shortcut: optional unit override for value.

atomic.description: true (default): all or nothing — any invalid item, refused value or read-back mismatch rolls the whole call back. false: valid items are written and the rest reported in items[] with their status.

allowCritical.description: Allow parameters that change what an element is or where it lives (type, levels and constraints, phases, workset, host) and one Mark on many elements. Default false.

tools.name: set_project_info
tools.description: Set Project Information fields (they feed every title block): name, number, clientName, address, status, issueDate, buildingName, author, organizationName, organizationDescription (by built-in parameter, so it works in any Revit language) plus extra{name: value} for custom project parameters. All or nothing; each value is read back and returned with the old value. Undo: Ctrl+Z or send revert[] to set_parameters.

name.description: Project Name.

address.description: Project Address (free text; line breaks allowed).

issueDate.description: Project Issue Date (free text, written as given, e.g. "2026-10-17" or "17/10/2026").

extra.description: Other Project Information parameters by name, e.g. {"Responsável técnico": "AE"}; same value rules as set_parameters.

tools.name: set_schedule_filters_sorting
tools.description: Set a schedule's filters (eq, neq, gt/gte/lt/lte with numbers in mm/m2/m3/deg, contains, begins_with, ends_with and negations, has_value/has_no_value; at most 8), sorting/grouping (asc/desc, header, footer, blank line), itemization, grand total, title/header/grid-line visibility and name. mode replace (default) or append. Filters and sorting only use fields already in the schedule (add hidden ones with modify_schedule_fields). Returns the definition read back. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

filters.description: Filters (AND, at most 8 in total) over fields of the schedule (hidden ones included). Omit to leave filters as they are; [] with mode replace clears them.

field.description: Field already in the schedule (it may be hidden): {name: column heading or field name} | {builtIn} | {guid}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

op.description: Operator. Numbers are compared in wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg).

value.description: Value to compare with (not used by has_value/has_no_value). Number in wire units, text, true/false, or a level/phase name for element fields.

sort.description: Sorting/grouping levels. Omit to leave sorting as it is; [] with mode replace clears it.

field.description: Field already in the schedule: {name: column heading or field name} | {builtIn} | {guid}.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

header.description: Show a group header row. Default false.

footer.description: Show a group footer (title, count and totals). Default false.

blankLine.description: Blank line after each group. Default false.

mode.description: replace (default): the given lists replace the current ones. append: added after the current ones.

itemized.description: Itemize every instance (true) or group identical rows (false).

gridLines.description: Show grid lines in the body.

newName.description: Rename the schedule (must be unique among schedules).

tools.name: set_titleblock_parameters
tools.description: Fill title block data in batch: per sheet, parameter values by name written to the sheet or to its title block instance (auto picks the owner that has the parameter). Uses the set_parameters engine: wire units, read-back with 'mismatch', atomic by default, revert[] returned. Title block TYPE parameters (shared by every sheet of that type) are not written here: use set_type_parameters. Undo: Ctrl+Z or send revert[] to set_parameters.

items.description: One entry per sheet, up to 500 sheets.

parameters.description: Values by parameter name, e.g. {"Desenhado por": "AE", "Data de emissão da folha": "2026-10-17"}. Same value rules as set_parameters.

target.description: auto (default: the sheet if it has the parameter, else the title block instance), sheet or titleblock.

atomic.description: true (default): any invalid or refused value rolls the whole call back. false: valid writes are kept and the rest reported.

tools.name: set_type_parameters
tools.description: Write TYPE parameter values (affects every instance of the type; result reports instancesAffected). elementId may be a type id or an instance id (its type is used). Same rules as set_parameters: guid/builtIn/name references, wire units (mm, m2, m3, deg, %), read-back with 'mismatch', atomic by default, critical parameters blocked unless allowCritical. Needs human approval. Undo: Ctrl+Z, or send revert[] back to this tool.

items.description: Writes to apply: one {elementId, parameter, value, unit?} per value. Up to 500 per call.

elementId.description: Element id or UniqueId, as a string.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: New value. Numbers in wire units (length mm, area m2, volume m3, angle deg, slope %); yes/no as true/false; ElementId parameters take an id or a name (level, phase, material, type); null clears text and ElementId values.

unit.description: Optional unit for this number instead of the wire default: m, cm, mm, ft, in, m2, ft2, m3, l, deg, rad, %, ratio, or internal (raw Revit value).

elementIds.description: Shortcut for the same value on several elements: element ids (strings), used with parameter + value instead of items.

parameter.description: Shortcut: the parameter to write on every element of elementIds.

guid.description: Shared parameter GUID. Wins over builtIn and name.

builtIn.description: BuiltInParameter enum name, e.g. ALL_MODEL_INSTANCE_COMMENTS. Language-neutral.

name.description: Parameter name as shown in Revit (in Revit's language). Fails with AMBIGUOUS_PARAMETER if two parameters share it.

value.description: Shortcut: the value to write on every element of elementIds (same rules as items[].value).

unit.description: Shortcut: optional unit override for value.

atomic.description: true (default): all or nothing — any invalid item, refused value or read-back mismatch rolls the whole call back. false: valid items are written and the rest reported in items[] with their status.

allowCritical.description: Allow parameters that change what an element is or where it lives (type, levels and constraints, phases, workset, host) and one Mark on many elements. Default false.

tools.name: set_view_crop
tools.description: Set the crop of up to 200 views: cropActive, cropVisible, annotationCropActive, a model-XY rectangle in mm (plans), or fitElementIds + padding mm (any view; projected through the view's crop transform), or a scope box ("none" removes it; a scope box overrides a manual crop). Returns the crop before and after, read back. Atomic by default. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

cropActive.description: Turn the crop region on or off.

cropVisible.description: Show or hide the crop region boundary.

annotationCropActive.description: Turn the annotation crop on or off (plans, sections, elevations).

rect.description: New crop rectangle in model XY (mm). Plans only (for other views use fitElementIds). Turns the crop on.

x.description: X coordinate in mm (project internal origin).

y.description: Y coordinate in mm (project internal origin).

x.description: X coordinate in mm (project internal origin).

y.description: Y coordinate in mm (project internal origin).

fitElementIds.description: Crop each view to these elements' extents as seen in the view, plus padding. Turns the crop on.

scopeBox.description: Scope box name or id to assign (it then drives the crop), or "none" to remove it.

atomic.description: true (default): any view that fails rolls the whole call back. false: failures are reported per view.

tools.name: set_view_filter
tools.description: Apply, update or remove a view filter on a view or a view template, with visibility, enabled state and graphic overrides (line colour/weight/pattern, surface/cut patterns, transparency, halftone). Overrides are merged with the current ones by default. A view whose template controls filters fails with VIEW_CONTROLLED_BY_TEMPLATE: target the template. Returns the overrides read back. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

view.description: View (name or id). Give view or template.

template.description: View template (name or id), to change every view that uses it. Give view or template.

filter.description: Filter (rule-based or selection) by name or id.

operation.description: add (default; updates if already applied), update (must be applied) or remove (from the view; the filter definition is kept).

visible.description: Show (true) or hide (false) the elements that pass the filter.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the filter in the view without removing it.

overrides.description: Graphic overrides for the filtered elements.

pattern.description: Line pattern name or id ("Solid" for continuous).
Line pattern name or id ("Solid" for continuous).
Fill pattern name or id ("solid" for a solid fill, in any language).
